column1: # depends on, the version it was verified at, and how.
# Several of our security properties are not ours. They are behaviours of an
# upstream project that someone read once, at one version, and then built on.
# Each was true at that version. None of them is a promise.
# A version bump is exactly the moment a vendor behaviour changes, and also the
# moment nobody re-reads the reasoning that depended on it. So the gate sits on
# the bump: this file records the version, api/internal/gatereg's test reads the
# version the tree actually pins, and a difference fails until the row has been
#   id          a stable key for the row.
#   version     the version the capability was verified at.
#   capability  what we rely on it to do. Specific enough to re-test.
#   verified    HOW it was checked - the column that makes this a record rather
#               than a wish. `unverified` is allowed and must cite a probe.
#   pin         where the tree pins the version:
#                 elsewhere:<repo path>    pinned in another repository; this
#                                          gate records it and cannot check it
#   cite        the issue or probe, required when `verified` is `unverified`.
# Do NOT edit `version` to make the gate pass. Re-verify the capability at the
# version the tree now pins, then write down what you did in `verified`.
